To Whom It May Concern,  

I had the pleasure of collaborating with Olumide Afolabi during a project focused on optimizing data pipelines for a game analytics platform. As a professor, I observed his work through a series of academic partnerships with NexaGame Studios, where he contributed to their data infrastructure as a senior engineer. His role required balancing technical rigor with cross-functional collaboration, a dynamic in which he thrived.  

Olumide’s strength lies in his ability to translate complex data challenges into scalable solutions. At NexaGame, he spearheaded the migration of their analytics workflows to Snowflake, reducing query latency by 40% and enabling real-time player behavior tracking. His ownership of dbt pipelines ensured data consistency across teams, eliminating manual reconciliation steps. These efforts directly supported the studio’s ability to refine game monetization strategies.  

A standout moment occurred when a Kafka stream bottleneck threatened to delay a major release. Olumide rearchitected the pipeline using Apache Spark, distributing the load across multiple clusters. His iterative approach—testing micro-batches and tuning parallelism—restored reliability without sacrificing performance. This problem-solving mindset was consistent: whether debugging a data quality framework or deploying Terraform templates for cloud infrastructure, he approached tasks with methodical precision.  

Beyond technical expertise, Olumide’s collaborative spirit and intellectual curiosity made him a trusted peer. He mentored junior engineers on best practices for data modeling and Docker containerization, fostering a culture of shared growth. His work ethic is defined by patience and attention to detail, traits that align seamlessly with both academic and industry demands.
